subject: Drafting approach: MSA/Order Form liability cap allocation and proposed language
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <procurement@helix-systems.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: sara.bloom@helix-systems.com, legal@helix-systems.com
Date: 2027-08-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Liability cap — preference and ask on drafting

Aditya,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. To summarize Helix's commercial preference on the liability section so your team can provide draft language for the MSA + Order Form:

- Cap: Helix prefers a single aggregate cap equal to 1x Annual Fees (we typically avoid multi-year caps).
- Measurement: Cap should be calculated on fees paid in the prior 12 months, not the contract term.
- Exclusions: we are open to the standard carveouts (breach of confidentiality, indemnity for IP, personal injury/death) but we want consequential damages excluded as a separate bullet rather than rolled into "direct" language.
- Insurance: we will provide proof of insurance; we expect Redwood to warrant that they maintain at least $5M general liability.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 1x annual-fees anchor and, if not, propose alternate anchors (e.g., multiple-of-fees or per-annum slice) and sample redline text we can share with our counsel?

Tom
Tom Reynolds
Procurement Manager, Helix Systems
procurement@helix-systems.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Tom Reynolds <procurement@helix-systems.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Liability cap — preference and ask on drafting

Tom — appreciate the clear summary. Short answer: we can get to a pragmatic compromise but need to balance commercial exposure and our insurance profile. A few notes and options for counsel: 

1) Why Redwood pushes back on a straight 1x annual-fees aggregate cap:
   - For multi-year deals, an aggregate 1x may under-index actual run-rate exposure and can leave customers under-protected if they scale quickly.
   - Our reinsurance/retention profile limits us taking an aggregate cap below a certain threshold for higher-SKU usage.

2) Practical alternatives (we can provide redlines for any of these):
   a) Per-12-month slice cap: cap = greater of $250k or fees paid in prior 12 months (limits peak-year exposure)
   b) Multiple-of-fees aggregate: cap = 2x fees paid in prior 12 months (balances risk/reward)
   c) Hybrid: 1x fees per annum but aggregate floor = $750k (protects us on small pilots)

3) Carveouts we can accept: breach of confidentiality, IP indemnity, gross negligence/intentional misconduct, personal injury/death. We want consequential/indirect damages excluded but would like to add a narrow carve-in for loss of customer data where remediation costs to Redwood are quantifiable (not speculative lost profits).

I'll loop in Laura (counsel) to draft the exact MSA/Order Form language. Marissa on finance is cc'd to confirm the dollar floors relevant to this deal. If Helix is willing to consider option (b) or (c) it would make the commercial team comfortable.

Next steps: Laura will send a redline with 2 options (per-annum slice and 2x-fees aggregate) for Helix legal to pick from. We can also provide a short note describing insurance offsets.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
+1 650-555-1198

From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@helix-systems.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Reynolds <procurement@helix-systems.com>
Date: 2027-08-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Liability cap — preference and ask on drafting

Thanks Aditya — quick clarifying questions from Helix Legal before we see redlines: 

- On the hybrid carve-in for data remediation: can Redwood commit to a capped remediation bucket (e.g., up to $X specifically for forensic/remediation costs) rather than an open-ended promise? Our counsel will want to see a number.
- Are the insurance thresholds you mentioned (our $5M ask vs Redwood's maintenance) negotiable? Please include the insurance clause draft and any certificate we should expect.
- Also, we rarely accept a per-12-month floor that effectively raises the cap higher than an aggregate approach for multi-year projects. Can the redlines clearly show both calculation examples for FY1 vs FY2 so counsel can see the math.

Sara Bloom
General Counsel (interim), Helix Systems
+1 212-555-0099

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@helix-systems.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-16T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Liability cap — draft redlines attached

Sara / Tom / Aditya — attaching two redline options (MSA section 12) and a short drafting memo. Key points in the redlines: 

- Option A (Per-12-Month Slice): "Supplier's aggregate liability for all claims arising in any rolling 12-month period shall not exceed the aggregate fees paid by Customer to Supplier in the prior 12 months; provided that such cap shall not be less than $250,000."
- Option B (2x Fees Aggregate): "Supplier's aggregate liability for all claims arising under this Agreement shall not exceed two times the fees actually paid by Customer to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim."
- Consequential damages: excluded expressly. We added a narrowly-tailored data remediation carve-in: "Notwithstanding the exclusion of consequential damages, Customer's direct costs reasonably and demonstrably incurred to contain, investigate and remediate a confirmed data breach caused by Supplier's breach of its security obligations shall be recoverable up to a cap of $500,000, subject to Supplier's obligation to mitigate and provided Customer produces reasonable documentation of costs."
- Insurance: we propose Redwood represent it will maintain commercial general liability and cyber insurance at commercially reasonable limits and to provide a certificate on request; if Helix requires a $5M specific limit we will escalate but expect a premium credit/commitment in return.

Attachments: Helix_MSA_redline_v3.docx (contains tracked changes), drafting_memo_cap_options.pdf

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

[Attachment stubs: Helix_MSA_redline_v3.docx, drafting_memo_cap_options.pdf]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-17T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Liability cap — next steps and ask for decision

Tom / Sara — thanks for the quick review. To summarize and propose next steps: 

- We provided two viable drafting options (per-12-month slice and 2x-fees aggregate) plus a hybrid data remediation carve-in capped at $500k.
- If Helix is comfortable with Option B (2x fees aggregate) or the hybrid with a $500k remediation cap we can proceed to finalize the MSA and sign the Order Form this week.
- If Helix requires a strict 1x aggregate cap and a $5M explicit insurance requirement without commercial concessions, we'll need 24–48 hours to run a pricing/credit adjustment and get exec approval.

Ask: Please indicate (by reply) which of the following Helix selects: "Option A (Per-12-Month Slice)", "Option B (2x Fees Aggregate)", "Hybrid (1x/Remediation $500k)" or "1x aggregate + $5M insurance (requires pricing)". If you want us to produce tracked redlines that reflect Helix's preferred path, say so and we'll send them.

Looking forward — happy to hop on a 20m call if helpful.

Best,
Aditya
Senior Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
